paragraphs.text: Spermatogenic failure-105 (SPGF105) is a form of male infertility. Affected men have reduced sperm motility and abnormal sperm morphology, described as asthenoteratozoospermia or oligoasthenoteratozoospermia. Their sperm show malformations of both the acrosome and the flagellum (Gao et al., 2025; Wang et al., 2026). Intracytoplasmic sperm injection (ICSI) has led to fertilization in affected men (Gao et al., 2025; Wang et al., 2026).

paragraphs.text: Wang et al. (2026) described a Chinese man with primary infertility and severe idiopathic oligoasthenoteratozoospermia. His sperm concentration was 2.0 x 10(6)/mL, progressive motility was below 1%, and vitality was 16%. None of his sperm had normal morphology: 76.5% had abnormal heads and 62.5% had abnormal flagella. His reproductive hormones were normal, his karyotype was 46,XY, and he had no Y chromosome microdeletion. Papanicolaou staining showed head defects, including microcephalic and conical heads, and tail defects, including short tails, acutely angled bent tails, coiled tails, and tailless sperm. Transmission electron microscopy showed acrosome defects, a disorganized helix of the mitochondrial sheath, and disorganized or missing '9+2' axonemal microtubules.

paragraphs.text: Gao et al. (2025) performed whole-exome sequencing in a cohort of 105 Han Chinese men with idiopathic asthenoteratozoospermia and identified ADGB mutations in 3 unrelated infertile men. One man was homozygous for a 2-bp deletion (c.2801_2802del), which caused a frameshift (p.K934Rfs*33); this mutation was confirmed by Sanger sequencing. A second man was homozygous for a missense mutation (c.3167C-T; T1056I). The third man was compound heterozygous for the T1056I mutation and a second missense mutation (c.3197C-T; A1066V). All of the variants were rare in the general population and were predicted to be damaging. In functional assays of the patients' sperm, the structural defects were associated with dysregulation of ADGB and of multiple spermatogenesis proteins. PLC-zeta was expressed normally, but calmodulin was deficient.

paragraphs.text: Wang et al. (2026) performed whole-exome sequencing in 781 Chinese men with primary infertility and identified 148 ADGB variants. Using ACMG criteria, they classified 45 as benign, 1 as likely benign, 96 as of uncertain significance, and 6 as likely pathogenic. Two of the likely pathogenic missense variants were found in the same man, who had oligoasthenoteratozoospermia. He was compound heterozygous for c.4859G-A (R1620Q) and c.4981A-G (K1661E), and both mutations were confirmed by Sanger sequencing. Western blot showed that ADGB protein was absent from the patient's sperm. On immunofluorescence, the patient's sperm showed clearly reduced ADGB and reduced staining for PNA, an acrosome marker. In control sperm, ADGB was enriched in the acrosome and in the flagellar mitochondrial sheath. AlphaFold3 modeling predicted that the 2 mutations alter the conformation of an alpha-helix and of a C-terminal loop, respectively.

paragraphs.text: Gao et al. (2025) reported that ICSI led to successful fertilization in all 3 of their patients. Taking this result together with the calmodulin deficiency in the patients' sperm, the authors suggested that ICSI rather than in vitro fertilization is the best treatment for ADGB-deficient patients.

paragraphs.text: Wang et al. (2026) studied a Chinese man with primary infertility due to severe oligoasthenoteratozoospermia (SPGF105). Using whole-exome sequencing, they identified compound heterozygous mutations in the ADGB gene and confirmed them by Sanger sequencing. One was a c.4859G-A transition (NM_024694.4), resulting in an arg1620-to-gln (R1620Q) substitution at a residue that is absolutely conserved across vertebrates. The other was K1661E. The R1620Q variant had frequencies of 0.0010 in 1000 Genomes, 0.0001 in ExAC, and 0.00285 in gnomAD. SIFT, PolyPhen-2, and CADD (score 28.2) predicted it to be damaging. ADGB protein was absent from the patient's sperm on Western blot. AlphaFold3 modeling predicted that R1620Q alters the conformation of an alpha-helix.

paragraphs.text: Wang et al. (2026) studied a Chinese man with severe oligoasthenoteratozoospermia (SPGF105). He was compound heterozygous for 2 mutations in the ADGB gene. One was a c.4981A-G transition, resulting in a lys1661-to-glu (K1661E) substitution. The other was R1620Q. The K1661E variant was absent from 1000 Genomes and ExAC and had a frequency of 0.0006 in gnomAD. SIFT, PolyPhen-2 (possibly damaging), and CADD (score 20.4) predicted it to be deleterious. Lys1661 is conserved in mammals but not in birds, amphibians, or fish. ADGB protein was absent from the patient's sperm. AlphaFold3 modeling predicted that K1661E alters the conformation of a C-terminal loop.
